solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stinking tide of rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb or adjective says the words tide of are worthless and to be thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A tide washing up rubbish makes a stink on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinking tide' reads as one phrase, but 'of' belongs to the fodder: the six letters of TIDE OF are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Foetid describes something with a strong, offensive smell; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Dandies transfixed by seductive bright lights

indicators.note: transfixed by says the dandies are pierced through by the seductive word

parts.note: fops are dandies
glam, short for glamorous, means alluring

explanation.surface: Vain dandies are mesmerised by glamorous bright lights.
explanation.definitionFit: Fog lamps are powerful lamps on a vehicle for seeing in poor visibility.

clue.text: They leave native lands, streaming abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters of streaming are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: People pour out of their homelands, flooding overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigrants are people who move away from their own country to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Borders of insular Asian nation

indicators.note: Borders of takes the first and last letters of insular and of Asian

explanation.surface: The frontiers of an island Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian nation' reads as the definition, but 'Asian' supplies AN; only 'nation' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Asks crew to pull nets closer

indicators.note: nets means catches, so the run of words Asks crew to pull catches the letters within it

explanation.surface: A captain orders the crew to haul in the nets and bring them closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' looks like 'nearer' but is a noun: something that closes.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-on lid is a kind of fastening that seals a jar or bottle, so it is a closer.

clue.text: Prematurely supporting gutless colonel, of course

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the word for prematurely beneath the other piece
gutless removes the insides of colonel, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: prematurely means early

explanation.surface: Someone rushes too soon to back a cowardly colonel, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearly and of course both mean obviously, without doubt.

clue.text: He chases European with scar tissue

indicators.note: chases means comes after, so the element follows the other pieces

parts.note: a pit is a small scar, as from smallpox
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: A man pursues a scarred European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a pronoun but is the chemical symbol for helium.
explanation.definitionFit: Epithelium is the thin layer of cells lining body surfaces, a type of tissue.

clue.text: Sock smell in teepee

indicators.note: in places the smell between the two letters

parts.note: teepee is read as the two letters it sounds like when spelt out, T and P
hum is slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A smelly sock is found inside a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sock' looks like footwear, but here it is a verb meaning to punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to hit them hard, which is to give them a thump.

clue.text: 9s, regularly missed, pushed up daisies discontentedly

indicators.note: regularly missed drops every second letter of pushed up, keeping the others
discontentedly empties daisies of its contents, keeping first and last letters

explanation.surface: Several of something died, as in pushing up daisies, unhappily.
explanation.walkthrough: '9s' refers to the answer at 9 down, POSEURS, so the definition is that word in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseuds are pretentious people, showing off knowledge they lack, the same as poseurs.

clue.text: Regrets surgery adversely affected individual

indicators.note: adversely here means turned against, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: rues means regrets
OP is short for operation, surgery

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having surgery that went badly for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' looks medical, as a patient affected by surgery, but means showy and insincere.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur behaves in an affected way, putting on airs to impress.

clue.text: Bash toenail badly and proceed unaided

parts.note: a bash is an attempt, as is a go

indicators.note: badly says the letters of toenail are put together wrongly, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone stubs a toe painfully and has to hobble on without help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bash' looks like a verb about hitting the toe; it is the noun meaning a try. 'badly' makes ITALONE from TOENAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is the idiom for acting independently, without assistance.

clue.text: Busy at home, oddly unseen

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of unseen

explanation.surface: Someone is busy in the house, working out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone line or room that is occupied is busy; the phrase means currently being used.

clue.text: It's hidden in Holy Land

indicators.note: hidden in says what sits inside the synonym for Holy once its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: holy means sacred

explanation.surface: Something is concealed somewhere in the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy Land' reads as one place, but they split: SACRED loses its ends. Acre is also a real city in the Holy Land, a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, and in the plural can mean land generally.

clue.text: Sherpa wickedly mimicked hippy

indicators.note: wickedly says the letters of Sherpa are given a naughty twist into a new order

parts.note: to ape is to mimic, so mimicked means aped

explanation.surface: A mountain guide mischievously imitates a long-haired hippie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' makes PEARSH from SHERPA. 'hippy' looks like the flower-power noun; here it is an adjective meaning wide in the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure shaped like a pear is broad at the hips, so the word describes someone hippy.

clue.text: Twitch and lie on Channel 8 broadcast

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the lie above the channel

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
a rill is a small stream or channel

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the number is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the number eight

explanation.surface: A twitchy viewer tells fibs about a programme on Channel 8.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel 8' reads as a TV station; they split into RILL and the sound of eight.
explanation.definitionFit: To fibrillate is for muscle fibres, especially of the heart, to quiver or twitch irregularly.

clue.text: Orphan found in empty paper bag

indicators.note: found in says the orphan is placed between the remaining letters of the paper
empty removes the inside of paper, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: Little Orphan Annie is the famous orphan of the comic strip and musical

explanation.surface: An abandoned child is discovered in a discarded paper bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Orphan Annie is the comic-strip and musical orphan; 'empty' strips the inside of 'paper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a bag or basket carried on a bicycle or pack animal.

clue.text: Yard with headless male chicken

indicators.note: headless takes the first letter off the synonym for male

parts.note: a fellow is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A farmyard holds a male chicken that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like part of the farmyard scene but is the adjective meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for cowardly, lacking courage.

clue.text: Possession of barbiturates eschewed by daughter with joint

indicators.note: eschewed by says the daughter shuns the drugs, so her letter leaves them

parts.note: downers is slang for sedative drugs like barbiturates
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Drug possession: a daughter refuses pills but smokes a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possession' looks like the drugs charge; 'joint' looks like cannabis but is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of having something as one's property, which is possession.

clue.text: Gold cases of incense, not all from the east

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: cases of takes the outer letters of incense, not and all

explanation.surface: Gold and boxes of incense, not everything shipped from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' reads as a phrase meaning partly, but each word gives its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means from or relating to the Orient, the countries of the East.

clue.text: County recoils after conclusion of vile deed

indicators.note: after puts the reversed county behind that final letter
conclusion of picks the final letter of vile
recoils says the county abbreviation springs backwards

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: A county shrinks back from the end of some vile act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoils' turns WORCS (Worcestershire, an English county in the West Midlands) into SCROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An escrow is a deed or bond held by a third party until a condition is met, a legal sense.

clue.text: Daub partner's droopy bits

definitions.meaning: wattle and daub is a building method, so the partner of daub, with 's
the fleshy lobes hanging from the throat of a turkey or chicken

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a partner's sagging body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Wattle pairs with daub in old wall-building, and fleshy wattles dangle from birds' necks.

clue.text: Crazy about new Royal, great beauty

indicators.note: about turns the synonym for crazy round

parts.note: nuts means crazy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a royal, the Queen

explanation.surface: A crazy story about a new royal who is a great beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses NUTS to STUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stunner is informal for a strikingly attractive person.

clue.text: Cycles back to front in protest

indicators.note: back to front moves the last letter of the cycles round to the beginning

parts.note: trikes are tricycles, cycles

explanation.surface: Cyclists ride backwards and forwards in a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of TRIKES moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a refusal to work, a form of industrial protest.

clue.text: Ran commercial about Slough

indicators.note: about turns the commercial round

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
to slough is to shed, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: An advert was run about Slough, a town west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a Berkshire town, but here the verb meaning cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to run quickly, so dashed is a past tense synonym for ran.

clue.text: Pedestrian Conservative's statement, full of endless rubbish

indicators.note: full of says the statement holds the trimmed rubbish inside it

parts.note: a Conservative would declare 'I am a Tory', a Tory being a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: endless cuts the last letter off the slang for rubbish

parts.note: bull is slang for rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A dull politician's speech is stuffed with pointless nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative's statement' is what a Tory would say: I am a Tory. 'Pedestrian' looks like an adjective for the dull speech; it means walking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambulatory means relating to walking, as a pedestrian is someone on foot.

clue.text: Lay hands on constable's sausage sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the words constable's sausage hold the letters

explanation.surface: A police officer's sausage is grabbed by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay hands on' looks like grabbing, but is the priestly gesture of blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest blesses someone by laying hands on them, a religious rite.

clue.text: Trio missing second plane?

indicators.note: missing second drops the second letter of the number

parts.note: a trio is three

explanation.surface: Three aircraft are flying, but the second plane is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' means the second letter, not a unit of time. 'plane' is the plane tree, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The plane is a kind of broad-leaved tree, common in city streets; an example of the class.

clue.text: See you make lace article

parts.note: to tat is to make lace by hand
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A goodbye note to someone off to make a lace item.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British ways of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Wild animal miles away from Maidenhead area

indicators.note: away from takes the abbreviation for miles out of the synonym

parts.note: maidenhead is an old word for the hymen

explanation.surface: A wild animal is spotted miles from Maidenhead, a town in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a Berkshire town on the Thames, but here it is the hymen.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a wild carnivore of Africa and Asia, an example of the class.

clue.text: Fifty one parrots piping eagerly

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
I is the Roman numeral for one
keas are New Zealand parrots
piping hot, so piping means hot

explanation.surface: Fifty-one parrots are whistling away keenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piping' looks like birdsong but means very hot, as in piping hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at once, without hesitation, hence with eagerness.

clue.text: Policemen essentially go their separate ways

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
per se means in itself, essentially

explanation.surface: The police officers, at heart, decide to split up.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter, each going off in a different direction.

clue.text: Swimmer, unclothed, held reproductive organ

parts.note: a carp is a fish, a swimmer

indicators.note: unclothed strips the outer letters off held, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A naked swimmer is caught holding a private body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unclothed' leaves EL from HELD.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpel is the female reproductive part of a flower, holding the ovules.
